# Independent cohorts with local LD

This benchmark evaluates standard BayesPrism, CDSeq2 (without gene-type prioritization) and CDSeq2 (with gene-type prioritization) on freshly generated synthetic individuals. It extends the nominated-variant experiment with realistic local haplotype structure and a rule fixed before test-cohort outcomes.

## Frozen design

| Component | Specification |
|---|---|
| Signal cohorts | Six settings, five independently generated cohorts per setting |
| Null cohorts | Ten independent 60-individual expression cohorts, each tested with 100 genotype realizations |
| Sample sizes | 60 and 120 individuals |
| Expression panel | 2,000 genes, seven cell types, 200,000 modeled-panel reads per sample |
| Target panel | 200 genes; a fixed family of 1,400 gene–cell-type tests |
| Injected targets | 40 genes in each of excitatory neurons, inhibitory neurons and oligodendrocytes |
| Nominal genetic fractions | $h^2=0.10$ and $0.30$, before expression normalization |
| Local LD | 40 windows from 503 European-ancestry individuals in the 1000 Genomes reference |
| Primary test | Bonferroni-adjusted minimum SNP p value per gene, then BH over the fixed family; $q\leq0.05$ |
| Prioritization | Frozen GAM6 top 40% within type: 80 of 200 candidate profiles |

The stress settings lower excitatory-neuron RNA abundance or increase expression heterogeneity. Window-to-gene assignments are for simulation, not actual gene cis-regulatory maps. Independence means new synthetic draws conditional on the same training-derived parameters and haplotype reference; it does not mean newly collected biological donors.

## Run native inference

Extract the archive using `python3 reproduction/reproduce.py independent-prepare`. The resulting `work/independent_ld/` directory contains:

| Path | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `FROZEN_SPEC.rds`, `cohorts.csv` | Prespecified settings and seeds |
| `inputs/frozen_parameters.rds` | Compact training-derived parameters, aggregate reference, target map and scorer |
| `inputs/haplotypes.rds` | Public-reference local haplotypes |
| `source_snapshot/CDSeq2_0.0.0.9000.tar.gz` | CDSeq2 source used in the benchmark |
| `dependency_versions.csv` | Recorded software versions |
| `code/` | Simulation, native inference, tests, metrics and verification |
| `results/` | Completed results that ship with the book |

The saved benchmark was run with R 4.6.1 and BayesPrism 2.2.3 at commit `19052052a6f30833b27e2148294459b0ba2f923e`. Install the archived CDSeq2 source in a separate library if you need to isolate it from your current package. The run guard verifies computational inputs and dependency versions. A byte-for-byte installed-library check is a separate, original-platform audit; independently compiled libraries need not have identical binary hashes.

```bash
python3 reproduction/reproduce.py independent-run --workers 4
```

This runs each cohort serially and parallelizes inference within a cohort. Caches and logs are written under `work/independent_ld/`. Interrupted runs can resume validated caches. A stale lock should be removed only after confirming its owning run has stopped. The generated simulations and native-fit caches are intentionally absent from the download because they are large.

## Read the result

At $n=120$, $h^2=0.30$, the reconstructed-input five-cohort results for excitatory neurons show 74 correct and 25 false calls for BayesPrism, 76 correct and 22 false calls for CDSeq2 without prioritization, and 50 correct and four false calls after prioritization. CDSeq2 precision increases from 77.6% to 92.6%, while full-target recall decreases from 38.0% to 25.0% and mean F1 from 0.506 to 0.388. Median expression recovery is 0.703 before selection and 0.847 after selection. The [main figure](figures.qmd#figure-6) shows accuracy and coverage.

The additional equal-budget audit finds contribution ranking performs similarly in this setting (92.7% precision, 51 correct calls). GAM6 improves precision over repeated random retention by 15.1 percentage points, with a paired cohort-bootstrap interval of 10.6–20.3 points. This supports useful prioritization, but not uniform superiority over simple support ranking. See [Figure 7](figures.qmd#figure-7) and [the diagnostic chapter](diagnostics.qmd).

This supports prioritization for more accurate candidate sets in the evaluated setting. It does not make every selected profile reliable: less abundant cell types and weak signals remain difficult, and fixed-threshold F1 can decline when recall decreases. Five signal cohorts per setting provide limited Monte Carlo precision. The supplementary figures show all types, stress settings and fixed retention sensitivities.

FDP here measures disagreement with **directly injected gene–cell-type effects**. Normalization can create indirect marginal associations, so this target is not identical to a statistical null of zero marginal association. The new full-family global-null rejection proportions are 27.7% for BayesPrism, 24.1% for CDSeq2 without prioritization and 10.5% with prioritization. These exceed nominal 5% and do not establish cell-type attribution FDR control when another type has a real effect.

Underlying data are provided in Supplementary Tables **S26–S35**. `TABLE_SCHEMA.txt` in the archive defines variables, denominators and workflow codes. The [1000 Genomes publication](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature15393) describes the source haplotype reference.
